attributes.has_name: PerceptionSystem detection lost due to processing fault
attributes.malfunction_description: A processor execution, data-transfer, or integration fault corrupts or suppresses a detection that the intended perception function would otherwise produce.
A scheduling, synchronization, or timestamp-handling fault delays an available detection beyond T_detection_window.
A health-monitoring or fault-notification defect leaves a failed sensor channel undetected and prevents the required safe-state response.
Power, compute, or internal communication faults cause complete loss of sensor data processing in the PerceptionSystem part.
Fault detected but system does not inform operator within FTT
WarningsSystem.handleTigerAlert does not activate audible/visual warning after detection

Following receipt of a valid confirmed tiger detection at detectionIn, one or both warning channels activate later than T_warning. Delayed notification reduces the time available for personnel to recognise the threat and take evasive action. This failure concerns warning-system processing and activation after valid detection input; it excludes perception/classification latency. Requirement: TDS_WRN_001.
WarningsSystem.issueTigerWarning produces alarm exceeding L_alarm_max — hearing damage risk

An audible tiger warning is emitted but falls below L_alarm_min at 1 m or fails to provide the required 15 dB margin above ambient noise under the specified operating conditions. Personnel may not hear the warning and may delay protective action despite a valid tiger detection. This failure concerns inadequate warning output; no particular hardware cause is assumed. Requirement: TDS_WRN_002.

An active tiger warning is deactivated before T_warning_timeout has elapsed since the most recent valid detection, without the specified transition to idle. A failed timeout refresh on a new detection is one possible manifestation. Premature clearing can falsely suggest that the threat has passed and interrupt protective action. Requirement: TDS_WRN_004 and the WarningsSystem timeout-reset behaviour.

The audible or visual tiger warning remains active after T_warning_timeout without a new detection event, or after the specified transition to idle. Persistent warning output can cause alarm fatigue and reduce personnel responsiveness to subsequent tiger warnings. This failure concerns warning retention and deactivation rather than an erroneous detection from the perception system. Requirement: TDS_WRN_004.
WarningsSystem.issueTigerWarning displays incorrect bearing/distance — evasive action misdirected
